issues.failure_explanation: The interior limit of the double layer integral is the principal value plus 1/2 beta, not u(x*)-1/2 beta. For constant beta=1 on the unit disk, the double layer integral equals 1 for interior x and tends to 1 at the boundary, while the stated right-hand side is 1-1/2=1/2 (taking u=f=1). The correct relation involves the volume potential or the principal value plus 1/2 beta, so the stated limit and the subsequent 'hence' derivation of the BIE are invalid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the limit equation by the standard jump relation, e.g. lim D beta = PV integral + 1/2 beta, and adjust the derivation of the BIE accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The limit statement in Theorem BIM and its derivation of the BIE are unreliable, although the BIE itself is standard and correct.
issues.title: False boundary limit for double layer potential
issues.why_classification: A short local correction to the limit formula preserves the BIE and all later substantive claims.

issues.failure_explanation: The Fredholm NN is intended to implement the Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration f_{m+1}=(1-kappa)f_m+kappa T f_m with T f = g + integral K f. The kernel terms in W_m and W_M should therefore be multiplied by kappa, and the diagonal should be (1-kappa)+kappa K(z,z) Delta z. As written, only the bias g is multiplied by kappa, so the network implements a different affine iteration than the one analyzed by the error bound that depends on kappa.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply all K terms in W_m and W_M by kappa and set K_D(z)=(1-kappa)+kappa K(z,z) Delta z.
issues.overall_effect: The constructed Fredholm NN does not match the analyzed fixed-point iteration; convergence and error guarantees depending on kappa may not apply to the constructed network.
issues.title: Fredholm NN weights omit the Krasnoselskii-Mann factor kappa on kernel terms
issues.why_classification: A local correction to the weight formulas restores the intended Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration without changing the main framework.

issues.failure_explanation: For the Helmholtz fundamental solution, the boundary value of the double layer integral is 1/2 + lambda integral Omega Phi(x*,y) dy (plus principal-value terms), not -1/2 + lambda integral Omega Phi(x*,y) dy. The sign of the jump term is wrong, so the derivation in Proposition semi-linear-pot does not follow as written, even though the final displayed representation uses the correct +1/2 sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign to +1/2 and adjust the subsequent algebra consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the Helmholtz potential representation is invalid at this step, undermining the derivation of the final bias term.
issues.title: Sign error in Helmholtz boundary integral identity
issues.why_classification: A single sign correction in the proof preserves the final Helmholtz representation and its uses.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition assumes only non-expansiveness, q<=1, but the bound contains 1/(1-q) and an exponent -(1-q)v_M, which are undefined or degenerate at q=1. The paper's Poisson BIE on the unit circle has kernel 1/(4pi), giving the BIE operator Lipschitz constant 1, i.e. q=1. Thus the recalled error bound cannot be applied to the Poisson case as claimed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State Proposition prop:added-1 for q<1; for the Poisson q=1 case, provide a separate convergence and error analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The error bound for the Fredholm NN approximation of the boundary function beta is not established for the Poisson BIE, and error bounds depending on it for lambda=0/Poisson are unsupported.
issues.title: FNN error bound is stated for q=1 although it requires q<1
issues.why_classification: The missing hypothesis is local for the proposition, but applying it to the Poisson case requires a new argument and leaves the advertised Poisson error bounds unsupported.

issues.failure_explanation: The potential representation has last boundary term integral partial Omega beta(y) partial Phi(x*,y)/partial n_y d sigma. The definition of D4 and the interior error bound instead use partial Phi(x,y)/partial n_y. Therefore D4(Omega) does not bound the discretization error of the actual term, and the coefficient in the interior error bound is for the wrong kernel. The boundary case happens to coincide because x=x* on partial Omega, but the interior bound is invalid.

failure_location.quote: D_4(\mathcal{A}) := \left\| \int_{\partial \Omega} \beta_{M}(y)  \frac{\partial \Phi(x, y)}{\partial n_y}  d\sigma_y - \tilde{\int_{\partial \Omega}} \beta_M(y) \, \frac{\partial \Phi(x, y)}{\partial n_y} d\sigma_y \right\|_{\mathcal{A}},

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine D4 with partial Phi(x*,y)/partial n_y and replace the corresponding coefficient in the interior bound by the norm of integral partial Omega partial Phi(x*,y)/partial n_y.
issues.overall_effect: The interior error bound in Theorem error-bounds-thrm does not cover the PFNN based on potential-limit-expression.
issues.title: Interior error bound uses the wrong boundary kernel in D4
issues.why_classification: The error theorem needs a nontrivial but contained correction of the kernel and the corresponding coefficient; the main bound survives in modified form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where for the last steps we recall that the normal derivative of the fundamental solution is non-negative

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces |D Phi| by D Phi by invoking non-negativity of the normal derivative of the fundamental solution. But D Phi is the difference of two normal derivatives, not the normal derivative itself. For the Helmholtz fundamental solution this difference can change sign, so the inequality and the subsequent use of the norm of the integral of D Phi can fail; an absolute value is required.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use |D Phi| in the estimate, replacing the coefficient by the norm of the integral of |D Phi| over partial Omega.
issues.overall_effect: The first-term estimate in the interior error bound is invalid for the Helmholtz case.
issues.title: Invalid use of non-negativity for the difference kernel D Phi
issues.why_classification: The proof needs a corrected estimate with an absolute value; this weakens but does not abandon the error bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds ||tilde u_n - u_n|| by a single PFNN error epsilon, but tilde u_n is generated by a recurrence that uses approximate previous iterates to form the source. Errors from earlier steps propagate and accumulate. A correct bound is of order epsilon/(1-q) (or a geometric sum), not epsilon. Thus the stated inequality is false in general, e.g. with a constant positive one-step approximation error and q close to 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by a recurrence summation, e.g. ||tilde u_n-u_n|| <= epsilon(1-q^n)/(1-q)+q^n||tilde u_0-u_0||, then add q^n||u_0-u||.
issues.overall_effect: The RPFNN error bound for semi-linear PDEs is not established and understates the accumulated error.
issues.title: Recurrent PFNN error bound ignores accumulated approximation errors
issues.why_classification: A contained recurrence argument gives a comparable bound with a constant factor; no global architecture change is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\partial \Phi(x,y)}{\partial n_y} = -\frac{\sqrt{\lambda} K_0' \left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)}{2\pi |x - y|} \big( y_1 (y_1 - x_1) + y_2 (y_2 - x_2) \big).

issues.failure_explanation: Using K0'=-K1 in the preceding formula gives partial Phi/partial n = sqrt(lambda) K1/(2pi |x-y|) times y·(y-x). On the boundary, y·(y-x)=|x-y|^2/2, so the correct expression is sqrt(lambda) |x-y| K1(sqrt(lambda)|x-y|)/(4pi), not sqrt(lambda) K1/(4pi |x-y|). The displayed formula has the reciprocal of |x-y|, which diverges as x->y and contradicts the later limit 1/(4pi).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the erroneous expression by sqrt(lambda) |x-y| K1(sqrt(lambda)|x-y|)/(4pi) for x,y on the boundary.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical construction of the Helmholtz BIE and PFNN uses an incorrect kernel, invalidating the reported Helmholtz numerical results unless recomputed.
issues.title: Incorrect Helmholtz normal derivative kernel formula
issues.why_classification: A local formula correction preserves the method, but the reported numerical Helmholtz results are unreliable until recomputed.
